subject: Clarify charging for mixed short chats + occasional long-context uploads (slabized billing)
messages:

Subject: Billing for mixed short chats + long doc uploads

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Stellar liked the latency profile. Two follow-ups from procurement and engineering on how billing behaves for our real workload: mostly short chat turns (~20–80 input tokens), with occasional long-context uploads where an agent ingests a 6k–12k token document for deeper analysis.

Questions:
- Do you bill per API call rounded to a fixed slab (e.g. 128 tokens) or do you aggregate per-conversation?
- If a user streams a long document in several chunks (we chunk at ~2k tokens), are chunks billed separately or recombined for billing?
- Any minimums or per-session floors we should expect that could make short-turn-heavy traffic expensive?

I've attached a small sample of traffic patterns (example-usage.csv) — the third column is the per-call token count. Can you give a sample invoice line for a week with 10k short turns + 120 long uploads (avg 8k tokens)?

Appreciate a concrete worked example so procurement and finance can map this into our forecast.

Best,
Olivia
Procurement, Stellar Retail

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@stellarretail.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing for mixed short chats + long doc uploads

Hi Olivia — thanks for the file and the clear example. Below is a concise explanation plus two worked calculations so your FP&A team can plug numbers into their model.

Short version (policy):
- Billing is per request after tokenization. We "slabize" billing into 128-token units for interactive/streaming calls — each request is rounded up to the next 128-token slab.
- When a single logical upload is streamed in multiple chunks but the request_id is the same (or marked with the same upload_id header), we charge on the final assembled token count (no double-charging per chunk).
- We maintain a conversation-level prefix reuse credit: if the identical prefix (first N tokens) reappears within a 12-hour active window, we apply a reuse credit of up to 75% on repeated input tokens for that prefix (bounded to the first 2,048 tokens of the prefix).
- There is no additional per-session floor beyond the per-request rounding to 128-token slabs. In short-turn-heavy traffic you pay the rounded slab per call.

Worked examples (rounded to slabs):
1) Short turns: 10,000 calls at avg 45 input tokens -> each call rounds to 128 tokens -> billed tokens = 10,000 * 128 = 1,280,000 tokens.

2) Long uploads: 120 uploads at avg 8,000 tokens -> per upload slabs = ceil(8,000 / 128) = 63 slabs -> billed tokens per upload = 63 * 128 = 8,064 tokens -> total = 120 * 8,064 = 967,680 tokens.

Combined billed tokens for the week = 1,280,000 + 967,680 = 2,247,680 tokens.

Notes/caveats:
- If you consistently stream the same document prefix for many users, prefix reuse credits can reduce billed input for repeated early-turn tokens.
- For enterprise commits we can negotiate slab size or commit buckets — e.g., a committed block priced as 1M-token slabs vs. on-demand 128-token slabs.

I've attached a sample invoice line (invoice-sample.csv) that maps the numbers above to line items. Sergio — flag if you want me to soften any phrasing for legal.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Kimberly — that's super helpful, thanks. A couple quick clarifications before we loop legal:
- For the 12-hour prefix reuse window, is the match literal token-for-token, or do embeddings/fuzzy matches count? Our ingestion pipeline normalizes whitespace but otherwise preserves text.
- If a long upload is reprocessed within 24 hours because the user asks for a slightly different extraction, does that count as a new upload (full charge) or a reuse case?

Also sending the contract draft back that our legal team started — they'd like the billing language to be very explicit about the slab size and the prefix credit. Attaching contract-draft.pdf.

Team — forwarding Olivia's questions and the draft contract they attached. Key asks from procurement/legal: explicit slab size and the exact prefix reuse definition (token-for-token vs. fuzzy).

Proposed legal-friendly language for the SOW (draft):
"Billing: Calls to the Redwood API are metered per-request after tokenization. On-demand requests are billed in 128-token units (each request is rounded up to the nearest 128-token unit). For streamed uploads that share an upload_id, Redwood will bill the assembled token count once (clients must supply upload_id to avoid per-chunk billing). Redwood will apply a prefix reuse credit when the identical prefix of input tokens reappears within a 12-hour active window; the credit applies only to exact token-for-token matches and is capped to the first 2,048 tokens of the prefix."

Ask: Tessa/legal — can you confirm this language is acceptable? Sergio — any pricing/commercial tweaks? Marissa — FYI and please sign off on escalation if the customer requests a different slab in the enterprise commit.

Thanks,
Kimberly

Kimberly — language looks good but a couple of small edits to reduce ambiguity for legal and procurement:
- Change "128-token units" to "128-token billing units (the Provider may change the unit size with 60 days' notice for new customers; any change will not retroactively affect usage already billed)." -> gives us flexibility during product changes.
- Explicitly call out that prefix reuse credit requires the client to enable "prefix_tracking" in account settings (we need an opt-in for telemetry reasons).
- For the reprocessing question: if the client re-submits the same upload_id within 24 hours and the assembled tokens are identical, we treat it as a reuse and do not double bill. If token counts differ or upload_id is changed, we consider it a new request and bill accordingly.

If you want, I can push a redline into their contract-draft.pdf and send back to Olivia. Sergio — confirm commercial OK on the 12-hour window + 75% reuse credit and whether we need to cap total credits against committed volume.

Tessa Morgan
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
